about: Controlled vocabulary for the editors' (Polotsky/Böhlig) German statements in the printed Kephalaia edition, and for the transcriber's own commentary. Each German formula is mapped to one id; the id is what the EpiDoc pages carry (@ana="#ed.ID" on gaps, #app.ID on apparatus entries, #tr.ID on commentary paragraphs). The German is kept here as the key to the printed formula; it is never transcribed into the pages. 'reason' is the EpiDoc gap reason the statement implies when it stands outside printed brackets; inside printed brackets the reason is always 'lost'. 'judgement' records how an ambiguous or inconsistent formula was decided, so that every page is encoded alike.

destroyed.judgement: Physical loss of the writing surface. 'vollständig zerstört' (28.24) is the same statement, intensified; one id. 'Rest zerstört' (44.5) is the same statement after surviving letters, as 'Rest abgerieben'.

destroyed-almost.judgement: The editors use both wordings (13.14–15 'völlig', 22.4–8 'ganz') for the same statement; one id. Encoded as a loss: the editors give no letters.

destroyed-traces.judgement: First met at 45.20–24 under a brace. The editors name destruction and say that only traces remain, without giving letters: a loss (destruction named). Kept apart from 'destroyed-almost' because the editors name the traces, as 'traces' is kept apart from 'illegible'.

de: bis auf ganz geringe Spuren zerstört
destroyed-traces-faint.en: destroyed except for very slight traces
destroyed-traces-faint.judgement: First met at 46.21–24 under a brace. As 'destroyed-traces', lower degree of the traces; kept apart on the model of 'traces' / 'traces-faint'.

destroyed-abraded.judgement: Combination of destruction and abrasion: a loss.

abraded.judgement: Abrasion removes the ink, so the writing is gone rather than merely unreadable: encoded as lost. 'Rest abgerieben' (19.6, 19.13) is the same statement placed after surviving letters; the position in the line carries the 'rest'.

abraded-heavily.judgement: Degree of abrasion; a loss, as 'abgerieben'.

smeared.judgement: Ink is present but blurred: illegible, not lost.

smeared-wholly.judgement: As 'verwischt', higher degree (kept apart like 'geringe' / 'ganz geringe Spuren'). 'Überschrift ganz verwischt' (76.16–17) stands centred in the two title lines of a kephalaion: one statement per title line, the whole line illegible.

smeared-abraded.judgement: Where abrasion is named the writing counts as lost (rule shared with 'zerstört und abgerieben').

illegible-abraded.judgement: First met at 44.31, a whole line. The parenthesis names the cause, abrasion; by the rule shared with 'verwischt und abgerieben' a named abrasion makes the writing lost, not merely illegible. Kept apart from 'abraded' because the editors' word is 'unlesbar'.

illegible-provisional.judgement: As 'unlesbar'; the editors expected a later reading. Kept apart because it marks passages they meant to revisit.

not-read.judgement: A statement about the editors' work, not about the manuscript: the writing may be legible. Encoded as illegible (nothing given), with the id preserving the difference from 'unlesbar'.

traces.judgement: Ink traces visible but no letters identifiable. 'nur geringe Spuren' (47.6, a whole line) is the same statement.

traces-faint.judgement: As 'geringe Spuren', lower degree. Inside printed brackets (21.4) the brackets decide: lost.

uncounted.judgement: The editors print brackets with blank space and no dots: a loss of unknown extent. The width of the blank is typographic and is not converted into a letter count.

open-bracket.en: lost, extent not counted (opening bracket only)
open-bracket.judgement: An opening bracket that is never closed and has nothing restored after it marks a loss of unknown extent: at the line end it runs to the end of the line; at the line start (21.6–11) it marks the lost beginning, and a braced statement beside it describes the rest of the line, which is encoded as a second statement.

open-bracket-query.judgement: Opening bracket followed by a question mark (14.15): a loss to the line end whose existence or extent the editors doubt; encoded with cert=low.

blank-probable.judgement: First met at 64.32, printed inside brackets after the last word of a section ('[ wohl leer ]'). The surface is lost (the brackets win, as for 'traces' at 21.4); the editors judge that it was probably blank, as at a section end before a new enlarged initial. Encoded inside the brackets as a statement with reason lost; not as vac., because the blank is not seen. Kept apart from 'uncounted' because the editors say what they think stood there.

conjecture.en: editors' conjecture (not printed in the text, or an alternative to it)
conjecture.judgement: All forms of proposal are one type; the strength ('man erwartet' vs 'viell.') is kept in the English note. 'Kaum …' (29.13) is a restoration the editors mention and doubt; 'korrigiert; gemeint ist …' (34.8) reports a correction in the manuscript and gives the intended form. Both are proposals not printed in the text: the wording and its strength go in the English note. 'lies …?' with a question mark (39.24, there with '… oder …?') is a queried correction: it is not encoded in the text; every proposed form is an apparatus reading. 'Erg. vorher [x]' (51.1) proposes words lost before the line (at the foot of the previous page); 'Auch x möglich' (51.1) offers an alternative restoration; a bare 'Oder [x]' (52.33) an alternative to the printed restoration; 'Lies vielleicht' (54.23) and 'Lies wohl' (76.33) are queried corrections like 'lies …?'; 'x von y, vielleicht z' (53.21) explains a word and proposes a restoration; 'x [y]z fraglich' (58.23, footnote printed '22') gives a restoration for a dotted gap and calls it questionable. 'Lies x oder y' without a question mark (81.24: ⲙⲛϫⲙⲏⲛ oder ⲙⲛⲧϣⲙⲏⲛ for ⲙⲛⲧϫⲙⲏⲛ) offers two corrections and chooses neither: encoded like 'lies …? oder …?' (39.24), every form a reading. 'Es müßte lauten: x' (97.2: ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲧⲉ ⲧⲥⲟⲫⲓⲁ ⲡⲉ … for the printed ⲧⲥⲟⲫⲓⲁ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲧⲉ ⲡϥⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ ⲡⲉ …) states the wording the sense requires over several lines, as strongly as 'man erwartet': a proposal, the whole wording one reading. None of them changes the text.

correction.judgement: The correction itself is encoded in the text (⟨⟩ supplied-omitted, or the corrected spelling); the apparatus entry records the editors' reading. 'x sic, lies y' (39.7) confirms the manuscript form and then corrects it: encoded as a correction; the 'sic' is kept in the note. A correction that only adds letters is encoded with ⟨⟩ (51.26, 54.25). 'Lies x statt y' where x removes something the edition prints (51.31: ⲙⲉⲛ for ⲙⲉⲛ̄, a stroke) leaves the text as printed; the corrected form is the apparatus reading.

confirmation.en: the printed reading is the manuscript's (editors confirm)
confirmation.judgement: Covers the plain 'so' and the softer 'scheint sicher' / 'anscheinend so'; the degree is kept in the note.

uncertain.judgement: Applies to the lemma words; their letters keep whatever sublinear dots the edition prints. '(Anfang) x nur unsichere Spuren' (90.19) says the printed letters rest on uncertain traces: same id, text as printed.

uncertain-strongly.judgement: The three wordings are used interchangeably; one id. 'Von x nur ganz unsichere Spuren' (90.15) is the same judgement on letters read from very uncertain traces: text as printed.

de: für … ist der Raum zu knapp
die Spuren scheinen nicht recht zu … zu passen
rejected.judgement: 'für x ist der Raum zu knapp' (41.18) excludes the restoration x because the gap is too short: x is the apparatus reading, the reason goes in the note; the text keeps the printed gap. 'Die Spuren passen nicht zu x' (43.5) excludes x on the evidence of the traces: x is the apparatus reading; the text keeps what is printed. 'die Spuren scheinen nicht recht zu x zu passen' (45.28) is the same exclusion, softened; the softening goes in the note.

traces-report.en: editors report traces of particular letters
traces-report.judgement: The possible readings derived from the traces are given as readings.

parallel.judgement: 'x wie im Boh.' (64.22: ϣⲓ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲙⲉⲧⲣⲟⲛ) points to the same expression in Bohairic: a parallel; the lemma is the printed words, no reading, the language named in the note. The text is unchanged.

grammar.en: grammatical explanation of a printed form
grammar.judgement: First met at 68.25 ('ϭⲁⲓ̈ⲧ Qual. zu ϭⲁⲓ̈ⲉ'): the editors explain a form (here the qualitative of a verb) without doubting or changing the reading. The text is unchanged; the lemma is the printed word, the reading the form it is referred to, the grammatical relation in the note.

stroke-absent.judgement: The text is encoded without the stroke.

de: Über der Zeile ist etwas nachgetragen
added-above.judgement: Where the editors give the letters, the text carries \x/ (add place=above); 20.25 gives none. 'x klein über der Zeile' (41.19: the second ⲛ of ⲛⲟⲩⲛ written small above the line) is the same case. 'anscheinend über der Zeile' (42.11) is encoded the same way; the doubt goes in the note. 'x oberhalb der Zeile' (52.16, 53.5) is the same statement in other words. 'üb. d. Zeile' (71.30) is the abbreviated form. 'Über dem x noch ein y' (75.9: an ⲛ above an ⲉ) names the letter written above but not which x of the line is meant when the line has several: the text is then left unchanged and the apparatus row carries x as lemma and y as reading, the ambiguity in the note. 'Über x zwischen den Zeilen: y' (82.25: ⲉⲧⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ written between the lines above ϩⲛ ⲛⲁⲓⲱⲛ) names words added between the lines but not where they enter the line: the text is left unchanged and the apparatus row carries x as lemma and y as reading (as 75.9). 'Hinter x klein über der Zeile: y' (90.17) gives words written small above the line after x that the edition does not print in the line: text unchanged, apparatus row with x as lemma and y as reading (82.25). 'In x steht y über der Linie' (90.3) names the place inside one word: \y/ in the text (84.4, 85.8). 'x in y übergeschrieben' (92.2: ⲛ in ⲁⲛ) names the letter and the word: encoded y with \x/ at its place (48.20). 'Über x etwas übergeschrieben' (98.8: over ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) says something is written above x without giving it (as 20.25): text unchanged, apparatus row with x as lemma and no reading.

erasure.judgement: The letters stand in the manuscript over an erased earlier writing (51.10). The text carries them as printed; apparatus entry only.

written-small.judgement: 'x klein' with no 'über der Zeile' (51.14 ⲁⲛ) reports letters written smaller than the rest of the line, in the line itself. The text carries them as printed; apparatus entry only. 'klein über der Zeile' stays added-above.

de: Die linke Hälfte der Seite stark abgerieben
Rechte Hälfte der Seite stark abgerieben
page-condition.en: state of a part of the page (e.g. its left half heavily abraded)
page-condition.judgement: First met at 62.1 (footnote '1'): a statement about the state of a region of the page, not about one reading. The text keeps what the edition prints (brackets, dots and letters already encode the losses line by line); the statement is an apparatus entry at the line the footnote is attached to, with no lemma and no reading, the region and the degree in the note. It is not turned into gaps, because the editors still print letters in the region. 'Rechte Hälfte der Seite stark abgerieben' (91, unnumbered footnote) is the same statement for the right half, attached to l. 1 like 62.1.

de: von spät. Hd. ü. d. Z.
added-above-later-hand.en: written above the line by a later hand

expunged.en: expunged by the scribe with dots
expunged.judgement: The scribe's own deletion: the edition prints double brackets [[ ]]; encoded ⟦x⟧ (del rend=expunction), not as an editorial surplus. 15.16 adds the cause (dittography from l. 18 by homoioteleuton) in the note. A footnote naming a deletion point ('Tilgungspunkt', 33.12) without printed double brackets is encoded the same way (⟦x⟧). When the editors only think a letter is deleted ('anscheinend getilgt', 33.22) the letter stays in the text as printed and only the apparatus entry records it. 'x, lies y, z durch Punkt oben getilgt' (92.5: ⲕⲱⲛ, lies ⲕⲱ, the ⲛ deleted by a point above) names the deletion point like 'Tilgungspunkt': the deleted letter is encoded ⟦x⟧ where the edition prints it, although neither the point nor double brackets are printed.

sic.en: kept as transmitted, not understood or a scribal error
sic.judgement: The text carries «x» (sic). 'x sic für y' (39.5) names the intended form without telling the reader to change the text: «x» in the text, y as the apparatus reading. 'x sic mit …' (42.4: 'sic mit Artikel ⲙ') confirms a form as transmitted and names what is odd about it: «x» in the text, the remark in the note. 'x scheint so dazustehen (unverständlich)' (44.21) confirms the printed letters and calls them unintelligible: «x» in the text, as 'sic (unverständlich)'. 'x unbekannt' (31.7) and 'Bedeutung von x unbekannt' (76.9) keep an unknown word as transmitted: «x» in the text, no reading. 'x statt y' without 'Lies' (94.12: ⲛ̄ⲛ̣ⲉⲩ statt ⲁⲛⲉⲩ) states that the manuscript writes x where y is expected, without correcting it: the same judgement as 'x sic für y' (39.5): «x» in the text, y as the apparatus reading.

running-title.en: the running title differs from the usual one

margin-line.en: one line written in the bottom margin, not given
margin-line.judgement: Printed below the last line in the text block; located at loc='bottom'.

de: Am Rande klein nachgetragen ein Satz in kleinerer Schrift, aber nicht lesbar
margin-addition.en: words added in the side margin beside a line, in smaller script, not read
margin-addition.judgement: First met at 87.4 (footnote '4'). The editors report an addition in the margin next to the line but give no text, because it cannot be read. The line keeps what the edition prints; the statement is an apparatus entry at that line with no lemma and no reading. It differs from margin-line, which is a line in the bottom margin (loc='bottom').

number-position.en: the chapter numeral stands (in the manuscript) above the named words
number-position.judgement: First met at 89.1 (footnote 1): the editors say where the kephalaion numeral stands, here above the running title ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲁϩ at the page top. A statement about layout, not about a reading: the numeral is encoded as printed on its own line; apparatus entry at that line with the numeral as lemma, the named words as reading, no change to the text.

original-reading.en: the manuscript first had another form (corrected by the scribe)
original-reading.judgement: First met at 94.10 ('Ende ursprünglich ⲁⲡϥ̄': the line end first read ⲁⲡϥ̄, now ⲁⲡⲉϥ). The editors report the scribe's earlier form under the printed one; they do not doubt the printed text. Text as printed; apparatus entry with the printed words as lemma and the original form as reading.

bracket.en: how an unbalanced or cross-line bracket of the edition is encoded

print.en: a printing observation: stroke shape or extent (measured), blur, specks, rules

layout.en: layout: ekthesis, enlarged letters, unmarked blanks, marginal numerals, turnover, chapter opening

reading.en: a letter-identification decision taken on the zoom

source.en: about the source images or the page's context
